node.lifecycle.sentence.created: The record exists and no machine has enrolled against it yet. Issue a bootstrap token and run the install command on the machine.
node.lifecycle.sentence.draining: Moving everything it can to other nodes. Anything holding a volume stays put and is listed for you to decide about.
node.lifecycle.sentence.drained: Everything that could move has moved. What is left is pinned by a volume.
node.lifecycle.sentence.suspended: The panel is not publishing to this machine. Whatever is running keeps running.
node.lifecycle.sentence.retired: Out of the fleet. Nothing is scheduled here.
node.sentence.disconnected: No control stream. Its containers keep running and it reconnects on its own; the panel just cannot publish to it in the meantime.
node.sentence.dockerUnhealthy: The node cannot reach Docker. It is retrying and it has deleted nothing - "cannot see it" is not "does not exist".
node.sentence.catchingUp: Catching up: generation {applied} applied of {desired} published. It reconciles every fifteen seconds.
node.sentence.unschedulable: Running normally, and taking no new placements because you asked it not to.
node.sentence.runningWorkloads: Running {running} of {total} workloads, all at the published generation.
node.clockSkew.sentence: This machine's clock is {amount} {direction} the panel's. Certificates and ACME break in ways that point somewhere else entirely; fix time sync on the node.
node.list.title: Nodes
node.list.description: One machine each, running sasayaki. The panel publishes desired state to them and they converge on it every fifteen seconds; customers' traffic reaches them directly and never passes through here.
node.list.flagged.title: Needs attention
node.list.flagged.description: Suspended, draining, out of touch, or running with weaker guarantees than the platform claims.
node.list.flagged.label: nodes needing attention
node.list.all.title: All nodes
node.list.empty.title: No nodes yet
node.list.empty.description: Nothing can be deployed until there is a machine to deploy onto. Adding one gives you a bootstrap token, good for fifteen minutes and one machine, and the three lines to paste into its shell.
node.fleet.isolationWarning: Weaker isolation than the platform claims
node.detail.tab.label: Node sections
node.detail.capacity.title: Capacity
node.detail.capacity.defaultDescription: What the node last reported. Placement keeps headroom, so a machine much past eighty per cent starts refusing work before it is actually full.
node.capacity.none: No capacity reported. The node sends its CPU, memory and disk when it connects, so this fills in as soon as it does.
node.capacity.ariaUnreported: {label}: the node has not reported this
node.facts.title: Facts
node.facts.publicAddressNotSet: not set - a domain has nothing to point at
node.facts.stillCatchingUp: Still catching up. It reconciles every fifteen seconds.
node.facts.dockerUnreachable: unreachable - the node is retrying and has deleted nothing
node.form.create.title: Add a node
node.form.create.description: This creates the record and mints a bootstrap token in one step. The token is shown once, on the page you land on, and it is good for fifteen minutes.
node.form.create.name: Name
node.form.create.nameHint: What you will call this machine everywhere, and what you have to type to delete it.
node.form.create.publicAddressHint: The address customers' traffic reaches this machine on. It is what a domain's A record has to point at, and it is not how the panel reaches the node - the node dials out.
node.form.create.tagsHint: Comma separated. Placement filters on these, so a service that needs an SSD can be kept off a machine that has none.
node.form.create.notesHint: For the next operator: whose hardware it is, which rack, who to ring.
node.enrol.title: Enrol this machine
node.enrol.description: Run these three lines on the machine as root. It checks itself over before it writes anything, so a machine that fails preflight is left exactly as it was.
node.enrol.multiTokenWarning: Issuing another revokes nothing on its own - the old one is still live until it is used, revoked or times out. Revoke it below if you did not mean to leave two.
node.enrol.step1.title: Write the token to a file on the machine
node.enrol.step1.shownOnce: This is the only time it is shown. Put it in token.txt next to the install script; the installer deletes the file once it has enrolled.
node.enrol.step1.argWarning: Do not pass it as --token=. Arguments are readable by every user on the machine through ps; the installer only accepts a file or standard input.
node.enrol.step1.noLiveToken: There is no live token. Issue one below - it is single-use, tied to this record, and good for fifteen minutes.
node.enrol.step1.tokenHidden: A token is live but its text was only shown when it was issued. If you no longer have it, issue a fresh one and revoke the old.
node.enrol.step2.title: Check the script against this hash
node.enrol.step2.description: Compare it by eye with the value the command prints. It is the SHA-256 of /install.sh as this panel renders it, sent to you over your authenticated session rather than by the download being checked.
node.enrol.step3.title: Run the installer
node.enrol.step3.commandWaiting: The command appears once a token is live. Without one it would install a daemon that has nothing to enrol with.
node.enrol.step3.details: It runs sasayaki doctor first and stops on a required failure, pins this panel's certificate on first use, and dials {endpoint} outwards - nothing has to reach the machine from here.
node.ops.title: Operations
node.ops.description: Nothing here stops a customer's containers. Draining moves what can move, suspending stops the panel publishing, and deleting only removes the panel's record.
node.ops.streamWarning: Draining and upgrading need an open control stream, and there is none right now. Suspending and deleting are panel-side and work regardless.
node.confirm.upgrade.title: Upgrade {name} to {version}?
node.confirm.upgrade.body: The node downloads the new binary, verifies its checksum, swaps it atomically and restarts. Customer containers are not restarted - sasayaki is only the control plane. If the new binary fails to come up, the node rolls back to the one it is running now.
node.confirm.delete.title: Delete the record for {name}?
node.confirm.delete.body: Nothing on the machine is touched: containers keep running, volumes keep their bytes and Caddy keeps serving. The panel simply stops knowing about it. Run `sasayaki uninstall` on the machine afterwards to remove the daemon.
node.reason.drain.title: Drain {name}?
node.reason.suspend.title: Suspend {name}?
node.reason.drain.description: It stops accepting new placements and evacuates every service that has no volume. Anything holding a volume stays where it is and is listed for you - a silent migration is silent data loss.
node.reason.suspend.description: The panel stops publishing to this machine. Everything already running on it keeps running, and it keeps serving customers.
node.reason.hint: Shown on this node's page afterwards.
node.reason.required: Say why. It is shown on the node’s page.
node.settings.title: Settings
node.settings.description: Placement reads the tags; a domain's A record has to point at the public address.
node.settings.schedulableHint: Off means the scheduler stops choosing this machine. Nothing already running on it is moved or stopped - that is what draining is for.
node.settings.notesHint: For whoever reads this page next.
node.doctor.title: Preflight report
node.doctor.noReport.title: No report yet
node.doctor.noReport.description: The machine sends this when it enrols and again on every reconnect. Nothing has arrived, so either no machine has enrolled against this record or none has reconnected since the panel started keeping them.
node.doctor.requiredFailedNotice: At least one required check failed on this machine. The installer refuses to write anything in this state, so a node reporting it either had the checks pass at install time and regressed since, or is running from an older binary.
node.doctor.emptyChecks.title: The report has no checks in it
node.doctor.emptyChecks.description: The machine sent a report with an empty check list, which means it is running a build older than the preflight suite. Upgrade sasayaki on it.
node.doctor.weaknesses.title: This machine cannot keep some of the guarantees the platform makes
node.doctor.weaknesses.gvisor.title: gVisor is missing on this machine
node.doctor.weaknesses.gvisor.body: Every container placed here runs under runc instead. A customer workload is separated from this host by the kernel and nothing else, which is not the isolation the rest of this panel implies.
node.doctor.weaknesses.gvisor.remedy: Install runsc, then restart sasayaki. Until then, keep untrusted work off this node.
node.doctor.weaknesses.quota.title: Disk quota cannot be enforced on {fs}
node.doctor.weaknesses.quota.body: Volume size limits on this node are advisory. One customer filling the disk takes down every other service on the machine, and the panel will still show their volume as within its limit.
node.doctor.weaknesses.quota.remedy: Project quota needs XFS mounted with pquota on /var/lib/wisper. Changing the volume root later means moving customer data, so decide it before this machine fills up.
node.doctor.weaknesses.cgroups.title: cgroups v2 is not enabled
node.doctor.weaknesses.cgroups.body: CPU and memory limits are what stop one workload starving the rest, and without cgroups v2 they are not being applied.
node.doctor.weaknesses.cgroups.remedy: Boot the machine with systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1 and restart Docker.
node.doctor.weaknesses.clock.title: This machine's clock is not synchronised
node.doctor.weaknesses.clock.body: It is {seconds} seconds out. TLS handshakes and ACME both fail on clock skew, with errors that point at DNS, at the certificate authority, at anything but the time.
node.doctor.weaknesses.clock.remedy: Enable an NTP client - systemd-timesyncd or chrony - and let it settle.
node.doctor.machineFacts.title: What this machine is
node.doctor.machineFacts.description: As reported at the last preflight run.
node.suspension.resumeConfirm.title: Resume {name}?
node.suspension.resumeConfirm.bodyCloned: Only do this once you know which machine is the real one. Resuming both halves of a clone puts two daemons on one credential, and they will fight over the same workloads.
node.suspension.resumeConfirm.bodyNormal: The panel starts publishing to this node again and sends it the current spec.
node.suspension.headerCloned: {name} looks like it has been cloned
node.suspension.clonedDetail: A node's fingerprint is its machine-id and hardware serial. Two addresses presenting one fingerprint means a running VM was copied, so both halves were suspended rather than having the workload quietly split between them. Decide which machine is the real one, run sasayaki uninstall on the other, then resume the survivor.

node.cloned.title.one: One node was suspended for a duplicate fingerprint
node.cloned.title.other: {count} nodes were suspended for a duplicate fingerprint

node.cloned.description: The same machine-id and hardware serial arrived from more than one address, which is what copying a running VM looks like. Everything involved was suspended and nothing was stopped: the containers on both machines are still serving. Work out which one is real, uninstall the other, and resume the survivor.
node.tokens.title: Bootstrap tokens
node.tokens.description: Single use, fifteen minutes, one machine. Only a SHA-256 is stored, so the text of a token cannot be shown again.
node.tokens.empty.title: No tokens issued
node.tokens.empty.description: Nothing has ever been able to enrol against this record. Issue one when you are at the machine and ready to paste the install command.
node.tokens.revokeConfirm.title: Revoke this token?
node.tokens.revokeConfirm.body: It can no longer enrol anything. If a machine is part-way through installing, its enrolment will be refused and you will need to issue another.
node.tokens.desc.live: Usable until {time}. It is the only thing that can enrol this node right now.
node.tokens.desc.usedFrom: Spent from {address}. If that address is not the machine you installed on, treat this node as compromised and re-enrol it.
node.tokens.desc.usedUnknown: Spent, from an address that was not recorded.
node.tokens.desc.revokedAt: Withdrawn at {time} before anybody used it.
node.tokens.desc.expired: Its fifteen minutes ran out at {time}. Issuing another is one press.
node.isolation.header: {name} is running with weaker guarantees than the platform claims
node.isolation.gvisor.title: gVisor is not installed.
node.isolation.gvisor.body: Every container placed here runs under runc, so a customer's workload is separated from this machine by the host kernel and nothing else. A kernel bug that gVisor would have absorbed is a host compromise here.
node.isolation.gvisor.remedy: Install runsc on the machine and restart sasayaki, or stop scheduling untrusted work here.
node.isolation.quota.title: The volume filesystem has no project quota.
node.isolation.quota.body: Every disk limit shown for a volume on this node is advisory: one customer can fill the disk and take every other service on the machine down with them.
node.isolation.quota.remedy: Project quota needs XFS with pquota on /var/lib/wisper. Moving the volume root means moving customer data, so decide it before this node fills up.
